subject: economics
title: Current and Capital Account
welcome_lead: Two halves of the balance of payments tell different stories.
meta_desc: A-Level Balance of Payments: current and capital accounts.
final_note: Trade balance, services, income and transfers all sit inside the current account.

concepts.def: Trade, services, primary and secondary income.
Investment income and wages from abroad.
Smaller account: capital transfers and IP transactions.
FDI, portfolio flows and reserve movements.

walkthroughs.body_html: The current account covers trade (goods + services), primary income (investment income, wages) and secondary income (transfers like remittances).
The financial account records cross-border investment - FDI, equity, debt, reserves. Persistent current account deficits must be financed by financial inflows.
Current + Capital + Financial accounts must sum to zero in theory - adjusted by a statistical discrepancy in practice. A trade deficit equals a capital surplus.
